title: Nanofabricated ultraflexible electrodes for chronic, high-density neural recording and stimulation
authors: Weinan Wang, Yuhang Ma, Pavlo Zolotavin, Liuyang Sun, Hanqing Wang, Kyu Hyun Lee, Kalman A. Katlowitz, Carter A. Kelly, Hanlin Zhu, Rongkang Yin, Yingchu Sun, Robin Kim, Luis De La Palma Piedras, Jiaao Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Xiaorong Zhang, Elizabeth A. Mickiewicz, Philip Adenekan, Nicole R. Provenza, Ganesh Rao, Alla Y. Karpova, Benjamin Y. Hayden, Sameer A. Sheth, Loren M. Frank, Lan Luan, Chong Xie
summary: Nanofabrication increases channel density while preserving small, ultraflexible neural probes.
introduction: We use electron-beam lithography to pattern dense interconnects on flexible polymer probes for chronic recording and stimulation.

heading: Parallel implantation of flexible neural electrodes
title: Centimani: An implantation robot enabling parallel, distributed implantation of flexible electrode arrays for large-scale bi-directional neural interface
summary: A precision robot implants flexible neural threads in parallel across distributed targets.
introduction: Centimani brings together independent positioning, optical targeting, and parallel insertion to place flexible electrode arrays across multiple brain regions.

cover.title: The parallel implantation robot
cover.caption: Thirty-two XYZ piezoelectric stages hold the microneedles in a 4 × 8 arrangement. The inset shows how the microneedles engage the flexible threads.
cover.alt: Thirty-two XYZ piezoelectric stages hold the microneedles in a 4 × 8 arrangement. The inset shows how the microneedles engage the flexible threads.

sections.title: Implanting threads in parallel
sections.description: The robot positions many flexible threads independently so a distributed array can be implanted in parallel.

sections.description: Optical registration and site-specific height adjustments guide the needles to their intended entry sites.

title: Ultraflexible probes with a custom ASIC for 512-channel recording and 128-channel stimulation
authors: Weinan Wang, Gerald Topalli, Xiaorong Zhang, Jiyuan Duan, Yiling Xie, Pavlo Zolotavin, Howard Wang, Lan Luan, Taiyun Chi, and Chong Xie
summary: A custom ASIC integrates high-channel-count recording and programmable stimulation with an ultraflexible probe array.
introduction: This system pairs an ultraflexible four-shank probe with a custom ASIC for simultaneous neural recording and patterned stimulation. The figures follow the SfN poster’s progression from hardware and bench measurements to in-vivo results.

sections.title: Integrated system and bench measurements
sections.description: A four-shank ultraflexible array and custom ASIC combine 512 recording channels with 128 stimulation channels. Bench measurements characterize the assembled device.
